Work / AgriLink Ghana

AgriLink Ghana

An agricultural marketplace on a PHP MVC framework I wrote rather than installed.

Coursework · CS415

PHP 8MySQL 8MVCTailwindApache
Source ↗

Problem

Farmers, buyers and transport providers each hold one piece of a transaction none of them can complete alone. The farmer does not know what produce is worth this week, the buyer cannot see what is available, and neither can arrange delivery without a third conversation.

Context

Built for CS415, a software engineering course, with the full engineering process documented alongside the code. Coursework — which I would rather say plainly than dress up, because coursework with a passing test suite is a stronger signal than a production claim nobody can check.

My role

[VERIFY WITH CLAUDE] — whether this was solo or a team project, and if a team, its size and which parts I owned. The record does not establish it, and I am not going to imply sole authorship of a course project by omission.

What I built

Four role-based portals — produce listings, price bidding, delivery tracking, and an analytics view — over a normalised MySQL schema.

The interesting part is underneath: the MVC framework is written by hand rather than installed. A front controller, a routing layer, and the design patterns wired manually rather than inherited from Laravel or Symfony.

Why these decisions

  • Hand-rolled framework, on purpose. The course was about software engineering rather than about shipping fastest. Writing the front controller and router by hand is how the patterns stop being vocabulary and start being something you can debug.
  • Role-based portals over one interface with permission checks. Four audiences with genuinely different tasks; a single interface gated by role flags would have collapsed under conditional logic.

How I tested it

The repository carries a unit test suite that runs on a fresh clone, which is the point — a reviewer can verify it themselves rather than take my word for it.

[VERIFY WITH CLAUDE] The exact test count is not stated here. An earlier version of this site claimed 43 of 43 passing; that number has never been independently confirmed, so it is deliberately not repeated until the suite is run and the output captured. This is the most checkable claim in the portfolio and it is worth verifying properly.

Evidence

  • Public repository, with the framework and the test suite both readable.
  • The engineering process documented alongside the code.

Limitations and trade-offs

  • A hand-written framework is a learning instrument, not a production one. It has no ecosystem, no security review, and no maintenance story beyond the course.
  • No live deployment. An earlier version of this site labelled it a live demo without linking one; that label has been removed rather than a URL invented.
  • Scope was set by a course brief, not by users.

Current status

Complete as coursework, and not maintained. The repository stands as the artefact.
